sources.cite: Fernandez J. Angioedema. MSD Manual Professional Version (full review and last update September 2026)
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP case clinic-swollen-lip-years-on-lisinopril, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: 'ACE inhibitors can directly increase levels of bradykinin'; ACE inhibitor angioedema 'is variable in onset and may occur soon or years after therapy begins'; for bradykinin-mediated angioedema 'epinephrine, glucocorticoids, and antihistamines have not been shown to be effective'; 'securing an airway is the highest priority'; 'Edema of the upper airways may cause respiratory distress and stridor'; 'The face and upper airways are most commonly affected'; it 'usually resolves about 24 to 48 hours after stopping the medication'. No dose is used in the case.
Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.
